text:
The Hockey Writers put it bluntly this week: "Sabres Need to Pay Jack Quinn ASAP." It is easy to see why. Quinn has 22 points (11 goals) in 22 games, scored twice as Buffalo ended a five-game skid against Washington, and now plays 18:53 a night, up from 15:39 last season, with time on 80% of the Sabres' power plays (37% before).

The breakout has substance. His own chances are up to 1.24 expected goals per 60 (expected goals measure the quality of chances) from 0.96, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at an 84th-percentile rate last season, with 54% of his shots off the rush.

The mixed part is his own finishing. He has 11 goals on 8.59 expected and shoots 17.2%, above his normal range. But his team has scored 4.6 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice, which has cost him points. Evolving-Hockey flagged defense as his weakness last season (bottom 2% of forwards in chances allowed), so watch the other end as his minutes grow.
